A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same NeuroMFA paper, including complete Appendices A–E. Text and graphics comparisons establish matching scientific content, with no material gaps.

before.justification: v5 reports original NeuroMFA analyses of Pythia checkpoints, architecture and training-data comparisons, and contaminated-data BERT experiments in Section 4 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v7 retains the same original empirical analyses and results in Section 4 and Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: NIN construction, SNIN sampling, multifractal spectrum computation and the emergence metric are unchanged, including Section 3 and Algorithms 2–6.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same language benchmarks, vision-model studies, standard-versus-deduplicated training comparison and contaminated-data BERT scenario in Section 4 and Appendices C–D.

E2.justification: No comparator is added or removed. The comparisons between NeuroMFA's emergence metric and conventional benchmark performance remain identical, including Figures 6–8, 17 and 25.

E3.justification: Both retain 64 sampled nodes per layer, lambda = 1 and gamma = 5 in Section 4. Model configurations, checkpoints, evaluation metrics and the 20% Wikipedia/80% random-data BERT setting also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The toy-network experiments, architecture and training-data impact studies, log-log validation and weighted-degree analyses are unchanged in Appendices A.2.4, C and D.

E5.justification: Both report averaging over 10 sampled SNINs, variance in Tables 3–6, standard-deviation shading in Figure 18 and mean/standard-deviation estimates in Table 9. Sampling and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted trends and qualitative findings match. This includes the benchmark and emergence scores in Tables 7–8, fit estimates in Table 9 and results throughout Appendices C–D.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Lemma 3.1, Appendix A scaling and self-organization derivations, and Appendix B complexity analysis are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: a neuron interaction network representation, NeuroMFA structural analysis and a structural-emergence proxy. Their claimed scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of spectral evolution and benchmark correlations are identical. Both retain Section 4.2's qualification about limited dataset coverage and Appendix E's acknowledgment that causality has not been established.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains identical pseudocode, model and sampling parameters, network-construction details and code-access information. No implementation or reproducibility disclosure changes.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, citations and reference list are identical. The positioning relative to prior emergence and network-analysis research is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v5 dated 24 January 2025 to v7 dated 6 August 2025. Body wording, title, authors, headings and document organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–29, Tables 1–9, algorithm displays, captions and page layouts are unchanged. The version/date stamp update does not change their presentation.

improvement.justification: v7 preserves the same methods, theory, empirical evidence, explanations, reproducibility information and limitations, including all appendices. The updated arXiv stamp and PDF metadata/link provide no meaningful net change in paper quality.
